answer.rationale: Write-path p99 degradation began shortly after a release went out 2 hours ago, making the new build the leading suspect; memory_b1 shows a rollback cleared a similar post-release spike with no customer impact, and rollback preserves in-flight writes since the prior build was stable. Regional failover (memory_b2) is the fallback if rollback doesn't resolve it, since the degradation is confined to the primary region — but failover during peak settlement write traffic carries higher write-loss risk than reverting the build. Capacity, circuit breakers, and read-replica routing don't address a write-path regression tied to a release. Verifying b1 and b2 to confirm rollback safety and failover as the contingency before committing.
